entries.title: Psalms 34:1
segments: Title, changed his behavior; or, more literally, changed his understanding, that is, feigned himself mad.
We always have reason to bless God, whatever may be our present condition; our mercies are great and multiplied, and our sufferings less than we deserve.

entries.title: Psalms 34:2
segments: Make her boast in the Lord; glory in him as my all-sufficient good.

entries.title: Psalms 34:4
segments: Jehovah can deliver his people not only from evil, but also from the fear of it; so that in seeking him they shall not want any good, but be kept in perfect peace and filled with joy unspeakable, their minds being stayed on him.

entries.title: Psalms 34:5
segments: They; who seek the Lord as their chief good.

entries.title: Psalms 34:6
segments: This poor man; David, who had been delivered from great and sore distresses.

entries.title: Psalms 34:7
segments: The angel of the Lord; the minister of God's will, sent to deliver all who trust in him.

entries.title: Psalms 34:9
segments: No want; of any thing which will conduce to their highest good.

entries.title: Psalms 34:11
segments: Those who know the blessedness of fearing, loving, and obeying God, are desirous that all others, especially the young, should experience the same benefit; and the earlier in life they become devoted to him, the greater ordinarily will be their excellence, usefulness, and happiness in future years.

entries.title: Psalms 34:15
segments: Upon the righteous; for their benefit.

entries.title: Psalms 34:17
segments: Supplication to God in trouble is the unfailing resource of his people, and they have blessed experience from time to time of his willingness and power to save.

entries.title: Psalms 34:18
segments: Of a broken heart; humbled and penitent for sin, and turned from the love and practice of it to God.

entries.title: Psalms 34:20
segments: Not one of them is broken; the meaning of this and other like promises is, that God continually watches over the bodies of his saints, as well as over their souls, so that no real evil can befall them.  Whatever discipline he sees good to lay upon their bodies, he will make conducive to their highest welfare; so that though it be in respect to its outward form an evil, it is turned by his providence and grace into a blessing.

entries.title: Psalms 34:21
segments:
vv 21-22. 
 
  Be desolate; the word in the original means, be held guilty, and, as such, be destroyed.
